sections.title: Sound of the letter a
paragraphs: You call this letter (a) /ɒ/. It makes a vowel, which is a sound made with open air. You hear it in (alma) /ˈɒlmɒ/, which means apple. This letter has only one sound in standard speech.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Drop your jaw low and pull your tongue back. Make your lips into an open oval. Turn your voice on so your throat shakes. Look in a mirror and check that your lips form a slight circle.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: This letter always keeps its single sound in every position. You say it at the start, in the middle and at the end. Hear it in (ablak) /ˈɒblɒk/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say this letter like the vowel in cat. That vowel keeps the tongue flat and spread. Pull your tongue back and round your lips slightly, closer to the vowel in lot.
